> But blender exports with _end bones, which have no weighting yet conveniently make the physbones easier to adjust the colliders for. However when porting to an FBX, these are gone, so I have to use an endpoint position. 

It depends.

Blender adds _end bones (leaf bones) to the FBX export, if you choose to check "Add Leaf Bones" during export. These leaf bones don't count towards performance ranking bone count (surprisingly).

If your Blender file already has _end bones as a result of FBX import into Blender, those _end bones now count towards performance ranking, even if you chose to uncheck "Add Leaf Bones" at export. The solution/workaround here is to remove _end bones from the Blender file before exporting an FBX.

d4rk's Avatar Optimizer tool is (gladly) smart enough about this, and can remove unused bones when "Remove Unused GameObjects" is selected.

@{68098a4626271974ef4d2775|full_name} That's true for the general bone count, but this issue is about "physbone transforms" not the general bone count, where _end bones do get counted.

Physbone transforms are counted on the final bone in a chain even if that final bone has no endpoint attached (meaning no physics are applied to it either). I have _end bones turned off on FBX export intentionally because I came across this issue.

Generally, on a physbone component, I have to go and ignore/delete any _end bones present as they count towards the physbone transform total, and fine tune an endpoint position to the physbone component that gets as close to the original as possible, which doesn't affect the total. Functionally it acts the same, but with less control over individual physbone lengths.

I've corrected my post to clarify that though.

details:
When prototyping new avatars or private avatars, I commonly use armatures which have _end bones, which have no weighting yet conveniently make the physbones easier to adjust the colliders for. The problem is how physbones count _end bones towards the transform total. By the time I port my model to an FBX, I remove _end bones and use "endpoint positions" on the physbone component instead. 

Most of the time this is fine, but in some cases a root bone physbone applies to two separate lengths. Such as a cowlick on hair sharing the same endpoint length as a longer strand of sideswept hair. No one will note the difference practically, but it's still difficult to adjust in 1 physbone root. Which can be annoying when trying to convert from my prototype to a publicly available model.

It would be a lot easier to adjust using a manually placed endbone, as each strand can have individual lengths to the collider of the final bone. However, the physbone component calculates 1 extra transform when a manual endbone is present. Even if the endpoint position being set to 0 means the final bone doesn't actually rotate. This is especially odd, as deleting the endbone, and replacing it with an endpoint position would have the same physics in game but count as 1 less transform on the performance calculation.

Here is a picture showing 3 copies of a physbone chain. The two on the left have the same properties except the middle has a endpoint position. The one in the middle rotates the fourth block despite not being treated by VRChat as having any more transforms. Both calculating as 4 physbones. The one on the right uses a endpoint position instead of a fourth bone, and is treated as having less transforms even though it rotates the same amount of items.

Changing this would make fine tuning physbone colliders a lot easier on root bone based physbone components, and make the need for individual physbone components less.
title: Physbones with "Endpoint Position" set to 0 should not count the final bone in a chain as a physbone transform in the performance calculation
